key_insight: Automated research agents scale better when they periodically forget past search history and restart from the best solution, rather than accumulating ever more context.
engineering_relevance: For practical AI discovery systems, memory management is a scaling lever: resetting agent state can deliver more progress per compute than simply running longer or adding more parallel agents.
method: Run multiple LLM agents with scored verification and inter-agent communication.
Periodically discard each agent’s session and candidate history.
Restart from the best candidate found so far to unblock further search.
evidence_signal: Across four tasks in heuristic programming, kernel optimization, and model training, the forgetting strategy improved results by up to 15% over parallel agents and up to 39% over a single agent.
watch_item: Aggressive state resets may drop useful context, so the restart frequency and what is preserved as the “best candidate” need careful tuning.
